newsitem.title: USA: US base metal premiums - spot aluminum/zinc firm.
newsitem.headline: US base metal premiums - spot aluminum/zinc firm.

text.p: U.S. spot aluminum premiums remain strong for nearby deliveries, but business further out was quiet, traders said.

A 1,000 tonne lot was sold for delivery in March at a 6.00 cent premium over LME cash Wednesday, and another 750 tonne lot of chain metal was bought by a trader at a premium of 5.25 cents for April delivery.
However, with chain metal, delivery is not guaranteed on a certain date.
But the high spot premiums were enticing certain consumers to sell some surplus metal. "Some small portions have become available this way," a dealer said.

Spot premiums for April delivery on small tonnages were also in the 6.25 to 7.00 cents per pound range, traders said, but premiums in the second half of the year were much weaker and business convering that period was quiet.
Zinc premiums were maintaining their strength at 5.50 to 6.00 cents per pound over LME cash. Traders said the next U.S. Mint tender would probably be in the second half of the month.

Premiums in the Midwest were said to be particularly firm. One trader based in the region said flooding along the Mississippi River has delayed progress of a few barges carrying metal from New Orleans to Chicago.
Some dealers with zinc metal on the barges have been trying to arrange swaps with other merchants to ensure delivery to customers, the trader said.

Lead spot business was quiet with premiums languishing in the 2.0 to 3.0 cents per pound range over LME cash as the backwardation on LME killed off any sales opportunities for the time being, traders said.
In tin, traders noted some tightness in Chinese material and certain brands of 50 ppm low lead tin, but overall supplies of metal were still good, leaving premiums largely unchanged from last week.
Despite the threat of a strike at Norilsk Nickel in Russia, there appeared to be no signs of U.S. consumers making any frantic efforts to stock up on nickel.
Premiums were unchanged from last week's 10 to 14 cents per pound over LME cash for melting grade metal, with small lots fetching higher numbers.
"The bottom line is that if there is a strike, I don't think it will be prolonged enough to interrupt supplies. Nobody is panicking," a dealer said.
Allegheny Teledyne Inc confirmed on Wednesday it was hiking stainless steel sheet prices by 5 percent from May 5. This comes on top of a 5 percent hike from March 6.
Traders said Allegheny's price hike was not surprising due to firmer nickel and chrome prices, but some were skeptical that Allegheny will be able to push through both increases in full.
